Welcome to Week 9. We are halfway through the 2026 NFL season, and this weekend features several intriguing matchups. The New York Giants look to build on their lead in the NFC East against the Philadelphia Eagles, who are starting a new quarterback. The Green Bay Packers look to upset the Patriots in New England on a special day as they celebrate Rob Gronkowski, and we have an epic showdown on Sunday night between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Chicago Bears. As we do every week, we collect all of the best picks and gambling content from CBSSports.com and SportsLine and put them in one place, so you can get sports betting picks against the spread from our CBS Sports experts as well as additional feature content for each game, including plays from top SportsLine experts and the SportsLine Projection Model, best bets from our staff, survivor picks and more. All NFL betting courtesy of SportsLine consensus.  Which picks can you make with confidence this week? And which Super Bowl contender goes down hard? Visit SportsLine, as its incredible model simulates every NFL game 10,000 times and is up more than $5,000 for $100 players on top-rated NFL picks since its inception.  Cincinnati Bengals vs. Atlanta Falcons (Madrid)  Time: Sunday, 9:30 a.m. ET (NFL Network), stream on fubo (try for free)  Open: Bengals -4.5, O/U 48.5 
"The Cincinnati offense is rolling, with Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins dunking on opposing defenses. Meanwhile, the Falcons have been struggling to run the ball as of late despite the presence of Bijan Robinson (48 carries for 200 scoreless yards in the last three weeks). The Bengals do provide an opportunity for the run game to get back on track (4.8 yards per carry allowed), but Dexter Lawrence has shut down other rushing attacks before. If the Bengals can keep Robinson in check, I'm not sure Atlanta can count on Michael Penix Jr. to go shot for shot with Burrow."Jared Dubin is taking the Bengals to cover the spread in Madrid. He and Jordan Dajani broke down the biggest games of the weekend here.

     Denver Broncos at Carolina PanthersTime: Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (CBS), stream on Paramount+ (click here)  Open: Broncos -3, O/U 42.5 
"Another week, another magical Bo Nix comeback. And you clowns wanted him benched! The Denver Broncos offense scored 15 unanswered points vs. the Kansas City Chiefs in the fourth quarter, and then the defense pulled off a goal-line stand against Patrick Mahomes to seal the deal. Amazing. Nix leads the NFL since 2000 with 9.1 yards per attempt when down by one score in the fourth quarter. He has 15 game-winning drives to his name, which is one shy of the most in a three-season span in NFL history. Nix hasn't even played three full seasons."This week, the Broncos take on a Carolina Panthers team that just fired their defensive coordinator and has some serious issues on the offensive line. Injuries are beginning to mount up front, and Bryce Young has been sacked 11 times over the last two games. Carolina is now tied for the second-most sacks allowed with 23, and up against an aggressive defense that ranks top five in sacks with 23. "You can question the Broncos offense all you want, but the Panthers defense has a weird issue with giving up a million points at home. They allowed 59 points to the Chicago Bears in Week 1, 26 points to the Detroit Lions in Week 4, and then 43 points to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 7. That's 42.7 points allowed per game at home."
Jordan Dajani is riding the Broncos again this week. His best bets for Week 9 will be published on Friday.

     Green Bay Packers at New England PatriotsTime: Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET (FOX), stream on fubo (try for free) Open: Patriots -1.5, O/U 46.5 "There's a good chance that there's no NFL team facing more pressure to win this week than the Patriots. For one, Tom Brady is making his return to Foxborough. For the first time since he was hired by Fox, Brady is going to be on the call for a Patriots game and this probably won't be the last time this week that you hear about this. The crazy thing is that Brady won't be the only Patriots legend in town for the game. Rob Gronkowski is being inducted into the Patriots Hall of Fame this weekend, so yeah, this feels like a game the Patriots can't afford to lose. They don't want to spoil everyone's weekend. It's fitting that Brady will be on the call because the Patriots' current quarterback, Drake Maye, has been looking a lot like Brady over the past few weeks. Maye has totaled three touchdowns in five straight games, which is the second-longest streak in franchise history. Brady has the only streak that went longer and he did that back in 2007 when he led the Patriots to an undefeated season. Maye also has seven touchdown passes of at least 30 yards over the past four games, which is the most in a four-game stretch by ANY NFL quarterback since 2019. When Maye channels his inner-Tom Brady, the Patriots are unbeatable, but the problem is that he also sometimes channels his inner-Tom Hodson. If you don't know who Hodson is, then just ask any hardcore NFL fan. If they don't know, then ask a Patriots fan who was alive in the 1990s. If you don't know a Patriots fan, then talk to an LSU fan. If you come up empty there, go to your local library and find the 1990 NFL Fact and Record book. If you don't have a library near you, then Google Hodson, but definitely do that last. I'd like to see everyone go through all the effort above because I feel like we're getting lazy as a society.Hodson started 12 games for the Patriots over three seasons and went 1-11 in those starts. During his time as a starter, he threw seven touchdowns compared to 11 interceptions, which I'm only mentioning because I feel like that's how Maye kind of plays whenever the Patriots face a good team. New England has played five teams this year that currently have a winning record: They've gone 2-3 in those games with Maye throwing six touchdown passes compared to eight interceptions. That's not ideal. So is Maye going to look like Tom Hodson or Tom Brady? Based on what I've seen from the Packers defense this year, I don't think the answer is going to be Brady. The Packers defense has been surprisingly good -- even without Micah Parsons -- and I think Green Bay somehow manages to find a way to spoil Gronk's Hall of Fame weekend and Brady's return to Gillette."John Breech is taking the Packers to upset the Patriots in New England.         The sellout crowd inside Williams-Brice Stadium held its collective breath Saturday in the second quarter after South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers was sandwiched between defenders on a sack against Texas A&M and had to leave the game with an injury.Sellers was slow to get up after losing a fumble on the play at the Aggies' 18-yard line, grabbing his left ankle before hobbling off to the sideline with the help of team trainers. Sellers re-entered the contest to open the third quarter during South Carolina's first possession and showed no ill effects of the first-half injury. Sellers exited the injury tent on his own power, slowly walking toward the locker room with just over four minutes to play before intermission."We're concerned," South Carolina coach Shane Beamer told the ESPN broadcast at halftime. "He's got an ankle, and he's getting an X-ray on it. I don't have anything else."
The Gamecocks (5-3), slotted No. 21 in the first College Football Playoff rankings on the heels of three straight wins, need their best player available the rest of the way to remain in the postseason conversation.Sellers was 10-of-15 for 151 yards and a touchdown in Saturday's game before leaving. Sellers has accounted for 13 touchdowns during South Carolina's current win streak and was named the AP's National Player of the Week last time out after registering 397 yards of total offense and five touchdowns at Oklahoma.
Sellers threw an 84-yard touchdown pass to DJ Black and a 79-yard toss to Mazeo Bennett to highlight his performance. Both plays were made off schedule with Sellers outside of the pocket."Those are great plays. I mean, you worry about those plays from a protection standpoint, so you see him get the ball off," Beamer said after that win. "And I'm proud of our guys, too. When the quarterback scrambles, it's not like everybody just runs around blindly. Like, we have a plan of what needs to happen when the quarterback scrambles, and we worked a lot of that on the bye week. "We talked about it this morning in our staff meeting: that, make sure we're big on scrambles because they're really, really good on defense, and they're probably going to get some pressure on our quarterback, and we've got a chance to hit some big plays in the passing game if we do. So, great to see those guys execute the scramble drills the right way.

title: MLB free agency: Six international players to know for the 2026-27 offseason - CBS Sports
description: There's no Shohei Ohtani- or Yoshinobu Yamamato-level player this winter, but there's still plenty of overseas ta
body:
There's no Shohei Ohtani- or Yoshinobu Yamamato-level player this winter, but there's still plenty of overseas talent available
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:18 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Major League Baseball's free agency period opened earlier this week and teams are now clear to pursue any roster upgrades they deem necessary. That includes players coming over from Japan's Nippon Professional Baseball league, South Korea's Korea Baseball Organization, and Taiwan's Chinese Professional Baseball League. Those are high-level leagues that have sent many impact players MLB's way over the years. Look no farther than the Dodgers to see how important international talent can be to a club. The Dodgers employed four different former NPB and KBO players this past season, including two-way star Shohei Ohtani, ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto, and starter Roki Sasaki. Ohtani was signed as an MLB free agent, but the others went to the Dodgers through the posting system. Per the posting agreement with MLB, posted NPB and CPBL players get a 45-day window to negotiate and sign with an MLB team. KBO players get a 30-day window. Players who do not sign during that posting window return to their previous team in NPB, CPBL, or KBO. The MLB team that signs a posted player pays a fee to the player's former NPB, CPBL, or KBO team.Here is the posting fee structure: Contract valuePosting fee$25M or less 				 				 				20% of contract value 				 				 				$25M to $50M 				 				 				$5M plus 17.5% of contract value over $25M 				 				 				$50M or more 				 				 				$9.375M plus 15% of contract value over $50M 				 				 				For example, the White Sox paid Munetaka Murakami's former team, the Yakult Swallows, a $6.575 million posting fee on his $34 million contract last offseason. That's $5 million on the first $25 million plus 17.5% of the remaining $9 million, which is $1.575 million. The $5 million plus $1.575 million equals the $6.575 million posting fee paid to the Swallows.   Unlike last lockout, MLB will not be pausing the signing window during the expected lockout, according to The Athletic. In other words, if owners lock players out on Dec. 1 as expected, that date will essentially serve as the same deadline for already posted NPB players unless the lockout ends before their 45-day window expires.There are no superstar-caliber players like Ohtani or Yamamoto available in this winter's international free agent crop. There are, however, several interesting players who can improve an MLB roster in 2027. Here are the six best NPB, CPBL, and KBO players to know this offseason. 1. 3B Teruaki Sato Top 50 free agent ranking: No. 4Possible landing spots: Cardinals, Phillies, YankeesJapan's Triple Crown winner hit .306/.383/.609 with 39 home runs in 2026. He has a similar skill set to Murakami but is not exactly Murakami 2.0. He doesn't have quite as much power (but has plenty of it) and won't walk nearly as often, but he does swing and miss a bunch and is unlikely to remain at the hot corner long-term. Sato is a very aggressive hitter who ran a 66% contact rate this past season. That is below the 77% MLB average. The consensus seems to be that he will land at first base or in a corner outfield spot if not next year, then soon. Murakami successfully overcame his contact issues to slug 35 homers in only 127 games in 2026 around a hamstring injury. At minimum, that will have MLB teams reconsidering how they evaluate the Japan-to-MLB transition. Like Murakami, Sato carries risk, and like Murakami, his power makes that risk worth the dice roll. The Hanshin Tigers officially posted Sato on Nov. 1.2. RHP Kaima Taira Top 50 free agent ranking: 19Possible landing spots: Dodgers, Giants, PadresListed at 5-foot-8, Taira gets outlier extension down the mound (close to seven feet despite his height), which creates a low release window. Hitters rarely see the ball come from where Taira releases it. He's not a gimmick pitcher either. Taira sits mid-90s with his four-seam fastball and backs it up with a cutter, sinker, sweeper, slider, changeup, and splitter. The sweeper and slider are distinct pitches, as are the changeup and splitter. The Seibu Lions used Taira as a reliever in 2024 and 2025, then started him in 2026, and he handled the assignment well. The breaking balls are just OK, and the fact of the matter is that pitchers this height don't often hold up under a starter's workload. I would assume the team that signs Taira will give him a chance to start. In the long run, though, he might be a reliever, perhaps even a multi-inning setup man. Taira was officially posted on Nov. 1.3. RHP Hiroki Itoh Top 50 free agent ranking: No. 26Possible landing spots: Angels, Giants, PadresA down 2026 season took some of the shine off Itoh, who won the 2025 Eiji Sawamura Award (Japan's Cy Young equivalent) after throwing 196 ⅔ innings with a 2.52 ERA. To be sure, Itoh pitched well in 2026 (3.18 ERA in 172 ⅔ innings), but he was not as consistently dominant as in the past. The 5-foot-9 right-hander is a seven-pitch pitcher with a low-90s fastball and the usual array of secondary pitches (sinker, cutter, curveball, slider, sweeper, splitter), none of which stands out as a plus offering. Itoh has thrown at least 150 innings in each of the last six seasons. He's seen as a crafty back-end starter in MLB, or perhaps even a reliever (Itoh sat 96 mph out of the bullpen in the World Baseball Classic). The Hokkaido Nippon-Ham Fighters posted Itoh on Nov. 1. 4. 3B Si-Hwan Roh Top 50 free agent ranking: UnrankedPossible landing spots: Marlins, Pirates, RedsRoh has an unusual agreement with the Hanwha Eagles. He signed the richest deal in KBO history in February (11 years and roughly $23 million), and as part of the deal, the Eagles agreed to post him for MLB teams this offseason, and Roh agreed to return to the Eagles to finish his career when his big-league stint is over. This past season, Roh, 26 in November, authored a .283/.360/.505 batting line with 29 home runs. He has real right-handed power and a good approach at the plate. There are concerns about his propensity to swing and miss as well as his arm at the hot corner. The Eagles formally posted Roh on Nov. 1.
5. RHP Kona Takahashi Top 50 free agent ranking: UnrankedPossible landing spots: Diamondbacks, Rays, White SoxThe Seibu Lions posted Takahashi last offseason, but he was unable to find a contract to his liking, so he returned to Japan for another season and threw 148 innings with a 2.64 ERA. Takahashi, 30 in February, is an international free agent now, meaning he does not have to be posted and can instead negotiate at his own pace. More of a ground ball pitcher than a bat-misser, Takahashi sits in the 91-95 mph range with his fastball and has two good secondary pitches in his slider and splitter. He also throws a cutter and curveball. Takahashi is considered a potential innings guy for the back of an MLB rotation.6. RHP Jyun-Yue TsengTop 50 free agent ranking: UnrankedPossible landing spots: Athletics, MarinersTseng pitched for Chinese Taipei in the World Baseball Classic in 2023 and 2026 and he has been one of the CPBL's top relievers the last few years. In 2026, he saved 25 games with a 1.80 ERA and 65 strikeouts in 52 ⅓ innings. Tseng's fastball typically sits in the mid-90s and has run as high as 100 mph in the past, though it has been a few years. His go-to secondary pitch is a breaking ball that needs improvement for Tseng to carve out an MLB career as more than a middle reliever.

Tampa Bay has won consecutive games behind a running game that has churned out a staggering 582 yards during the winning streak. Here's how you can follow the action, along with a breakdown and a prediction. Where to watch Bears vs. Buccaneers liveWhen: Sunday, Nov. 8 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ETWhere: Soldier Field -- Chicago, Illinois TV: NBC | Stream: fuboFollow:  CBS Sports AppOdds: Bears -3.5, O/U 48.5 (via DraftKings Sportsbook)Bears vs. Buccaneers: Need to know Bears red-hot offense Chicago's offense has been a juggernaut since Caleb Williams returned from injury. Over that span, they've scored 31, 30 and 34 points while receiving stellar play from Williams, who has re-entered the league MVP conversation. Over the last three games, Williams has completed a staggering 73.8% of his passes with four touchdowns and zero picks while averaging 287 yards per game. 
The Simmons effect Last Sunday was Jeffery Simmons' first game as a Bear after he was traded from Tennessee. Against the Seahawks, Simmons filled the stat sheet with six tackles (including one for loss), a sack and a pass breakup. Simmons was part of a Bears defense that held Seattle to just 17 points, 18 first downs and 252 yards. 
Tampa 2 Williams will have to rise to the challenge of facing a Buccaneer defense that is conjuring up memories of Tampa Bay's legendary "Tampa 2" unit. Over the last two games, the Buccaneers' defense has allowed just 13 points and forced a whopping eight turnovers. They've been especially stout against the pass, allowing just 175 and 125 yards in their last two games. Tampa Bay has also held their last two opponents (the Panthers and Falcons) to under 100 rushing yards, which is significant given the running backs (Chuba Hubbard and Bijan Robinson) they've faced in recent weeks. 
The Buccaneers' defensive charge has been led by linebackers Josiah Trotter (68 tackles and a pick-six), Alex Anzalone (42 tackles and three interceptions) and pass rushers David Walker and YaYa Diaby. Ground and poundAlong with their defense, the Buccaneers' recent success has been predicated on the running game and specifically running backs Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell. Tampa Bay ran for 258 yards in its 43-13 win over Carolina and 324 in the rain during last Sunday's 16-0 win over Atlanta while becoming the first team since 1974 to win a game without completing a pass. Irving ran for a career-high 170 yards against Atlanta while recording his third 100-yard rushing performance in Tampa Bay's last four games. Gainwell ran for a career-high 140 yards and 25 carries against the Falcons. 
Prediction After a 0-4 start, Tampa Bay has proven to be a team on the rise over the past month. The Buccaneers are first in the NFL in both rushing yards gained and fewest rushing yards allowed. Tampa Bay's passing game, however, has largely been non-existent, even with the return of Baker Mayfield. Until Tampa Bay's passing game starts to show its teeth, it's going to be hard to pick them in matchups like this. I'm picking the Bears in a game that will likely come down to defense and Caleb Williams making a few key completions down the stretch. Score: Bears 20, Buccaneers 16

        The Kyle Whittingham era in Ann Arbor got off to an inauspicious start as the Michigan Wolverines needed a miraculous (and controversial) Hail Mary just to beat Western Michigan in their opener. Things briefly stabilized with a win over Oklahoma, but the Wolverines hit a new low on Saturday night when they lost 15-6 at home to rival Michigan State. Whittingham arrived at Michigan late in the coaching carousel after Sherrone Moore was fired after an investigation into an inappropriate relationship with a staffer. The longtime coach at Utah stepped down in Salt Lake City after 20 years as the Utes' coach -- and more than 30 years on the Utah staff -- and arrived at Michigan tasked with resetting the culture in Ann Arbor. As an outsider to the Michigan program, Whittingham needed to win over some in the fan base by proving he still has what it takes to make a team a contender, but his first season in charge has done little to quell concerns that he's past his prime as a program builder. Michigan fans are already antsy about the program falling from its perch in the Big Ten's top tier, and even though it's Whittingham's first year in charge, the expectation was that the veteran coach would bring stability and discipline. Instead, the Wolverines have been sloppy and ineffective on offense -- no matter which quarterback is under center -- and while the defense remains stout, it cannot make up for their offensive ineptitude. That has raised the temperature under Whittingham considerably, and some Wolverines fans have already seen enough. 
Unlike some other programs that have to strongly weigh the financial pros and cons of moving on from an embattled coach, Whittingham's contract seemed designed to allow Michigan to pull the plug whenever they felt they needed to. Not all losses are created equal, and after handing their in-state rivals their first Big Ten win of Pat Fitzgerald's first season in charge, chatter about Whittingham's job will pick up considerably. Kyle Whittingham buyout, contract detailsWhittingham signed a five-year, $41 million contract this offseason to take over the Wolverines, which is a relative bargain for a program with deep pockets like Michigan. His buyout percentage is also quite low at 75% (one of the lowest in the Big Ten), which means the Wolverines could move on from Whittingham after just one season in charge for the price of $24.75 million.Given that a new athletic director will take over at Michigan in 2027 after Warde Manuel steps down, Whittingham will not have much institutional backing and will need to see the Wolverines improve considerably if he's going to make it to a second year in charge. His hire already felt like a stopgap after the sudden dismissal of Moore, but the hope was he could rebuild a culture of winning to set Michigan's next coach up for immediate success. 
Instead, Michigan now has to consider whether it's worth continuing Whittingham's tenure and trying to find a new quarterback in the portal, or whether it wants to bite the bullet on around $25 million to become the best job on the market this offseason (at least so far).

title: Ohio State's catastrophic 2026 season has lost Ryan Day his championship goodwill -- now comes the reckoning - CBS Sports
description: Julian Sayin's injury explains some of Ohio State's pain, but it doesn't explain a $40 million roster looking thi
body:
Julian Sayin's injury explains some of Ohio State's pain, but it doesn't explain a $40 million roster looking this lost -- or how Day plans to fix it
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:12 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        COLUMBUS, Ohio -- The despondent Ohio State fans who began streaming toward the exits with 12:51 remaining in the game -- on the heels of a sack taken by overwhelmed quarterback Luke Fahey on the wrong side of the 50 -- surely knew an unfortunate truth. The calendar may only read Nov. 7, but Ohio State's 2026 season is over. The legitimate title aspirations that come with being the preseason No. 1 overall team have been destroyed. No. 23 Oregon delivered the final blow to No. 12 OSU's College Football Playoff hopes in a 41-28 win that was much worse than the final score would suggest. At one point Oregon scored 38 consecutive points, the first time since 1999 the Buckeyes gave up that many points in a row. By the end of the game, all you could see inside The Shoe were green Oregon jerseys and jackets as Ducks fans made their way down to the bottom of the stadium to celebrate the road upset victory. "We didn't expect any of this to happen," Ohio State coach Ryan Day said. Day looked bewildered and lost when Oregon coach Dan Lanning pantsed him on a gutsy fake punt play call on 4th-and-10 from the Ducks' 37-yard line. Down 14-3 with little working offensively, it was the high-risk, high-reward call that the great coaches make, and shades of something Lanning may have learned from Kirby Smart. 
The dice roll near the end of the first half ignited an Oregon team that scored 14 points in less than two minutes and took a stunning 17-14 lead into halftime. Ohio State would not lead again. 
The defeat guaranteed Ohio State three losses on or before Nov. 7 for the first time since interim coach Luke Fickell's ill-fated 2011 season. The free-falling Buckeyes are 6-3 with games remaining against Northwestern, Nebraska and Michigan. Before the season began, multiple rival personnel executives and talent evaluators highlighted Ohio State as the most talented team in the country. Against Oregon, Ohio State looked like a team with a few stars (namely Jeremiah Smith) and a lot of players who could be classified as just another guy. 
For a roster that is among the most expensive in the country (more than $40 million, according to CBS Sports sources), this was completely unacceptable. And it is sure to crank up the fan conversation again on whether Day is the right man to guide the Ohio State program. The grace period from the 2024 national championship is now officially over. The OSU coach told his team in the postgame locker room it'll have to "weather the storm" that was coming. The Buckeyes are 6-5 in their last 11 games. That might work in College Park and West Lafayette, but it doesn't play in Columbus. 
"Not some place we thought we'd be," Day said. "Beyond disappointed. Understand what the expectations are ... your expectation is to win every game here. To lose three games is unacceptable, and I own that. That's never going to change from my point of view."The loss of starting quarterback Julian Sayin is a clear factor there, particularly with the last two losses, but it doesn't explain why the run game is putrid. It doesn't negate the fact the defense was completely incapable of getting a stop in the second half of a must-win game against the Ducks. That an all-world talent like Smith may never win the Biletnikoff Award as the nation's top receiver, let alone the Heisman Trophy, is as abject a failure as Day has had in his eight seasons as the Buckeyes' head coach. How badly Ohio State has looked without Sayin has amplified how little success Day has had in developing high school quarterback recruits. That Day would continue to stick with Fahey, the 3-star prospect, who looked OK in the first half before struggling in the second, and the limitations it places on the offense, is an indictment on a staff that hasn't developed a viable alternative. Sophomore quarterback Tavien St. Clair was a top-five overall recruit and yet clearly the staff didn't trust him enough to play him against either USC or Oregon. Ohio State did not enter the 2026 season with an tolerable solution in the event Sayin went down, and his expected absence for the rest of the season means the team has zero chance -- none -- of winning big without him. 
Day has found himself with his back against the wall before and found a way out. It got ugly after a home loss to Michigan in 2024, and yet the team regrouped and went on a playoff run to win a national title.While a playoff run is technically still a possibility, it's not happening. Neither is another Big Ten Championship appearance. The Buckeyes look destined for the kind of bowl game their fans will have little interest in attending. The dream 2026 season has turned into a nightmare. The big question centers on how Day turns the tide on a wave of negative momentum. 
Is it bringing back Sayin for another year? Is it making major staff moves at one or both the coordinator spots? Is it an all-in aggressive transfer portal approach to replenish the star power on a team that will surely be without Smith next season? On both sides of the ball, Ohio State wasn't able to properly replenish the ranks after losing four top 15 draft picks (linebacker Arvell Reese, receiver Carnell Tate, linebacker Sonny Styles and safety Caleb Downs) off last year's team. Next year's receivers room, long the best in the nation, looks respite of the typical talent you expect at Ohio State. On a bleak Saturday afternoon inside Ohio Stadium, Ohio State fans in droves turned their backs on what they had hoped could be another national champion. Day, in the next few weeks and months, needs to find a way to give his fanbase a reason to hope for better moving forward. The disappointment of this season casts doubt on whether he can.

schema.headline: Ohio State's catastrophic 2026 season has lost Ryan Day his championship goodwill -- now comes the reckoning - CBS Sports

title: Falcons vs. Bengals: Cincinnati seeks first international win as division contenders travel to Madrid - CBS Sports
description: The NFL returns to Spain for the second straight season with a matchup that features ma
body:
The NFL returns to Spain for the second straight season with a matchup that features many of the league's top offensive stars
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:01 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        Following a week without an international game, the NFL heads back overseas in Week 9 when it sends the Atlanta Falcons and Cincinnati Bengals to Spain. The Bernabéu will play host to American football for the second time in as many years as two divisional contenders descend upon Madrid.The Bengals are in search of their first win away from American soil in franchise history after going 0-1-1 in their previous two opportunities (the most recent contest dating back to 2019), while the Falcons seek to improve to .500 in games abroad. Atlanta is 2-3 away from the United States and last season lost in Berlin.This contest pits one of the league's hottest teams against a squad that aims to reestablish positive momentum. Cincinnati rides a three-game win streak into the Madrid Game and scored no fewer than 31 points in any of those triumphs, albeit with two of the matchups coming against bottom-tier competition. Atlanta, on the other hand, lost in two of its last three outings and went scoreless in its most recent showing.
Both sides are alive and well in their respective divisions, but the context between the two differs greatly. The Falcons are just a half game back of first place in the NFC South, which may be the weakest division in football with no teams at or above .500 through the season's first two months. The Bengals' position at half a game out of the AFC North lead is the superior standing considering three teams own winning records.Where to watch Falcons vs. Bengals liveDate: Sunday, Nov. 8 | Time: 9:30 a.m. ETLocation: Bernabéu (Madrid)TV: NFL Network, stream on fuboFollow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Bengals -3, O/U 52.5 via DraftKings SportsbookFalcons vs. Bengals key storylinesBijan Robinson and Drake London see bounce-back opportunity: It is no small feat to keep one of the NFL's top running back-wide receiver tandems in check, but how much credit do the Tampa Bay Buccaneers deserve for doing so in Week 8? With due respect to a formidable defense, the weather in that shutout might have had more to do with the Falcons going scoreless than anything else. A major one-week swing could be in store for this duo as it squares off against a Cincinnati unit that just allowed the Tennessee Titans to rack up 36 points. Robinson remains the league's rushing leader with 780 yards on the year, and London stands sixth in receiving yards at 624. If the Bengals could not keep the Titans in check, they will have their hands even more full with these two stars.Tee Higgins reaches new echelon: Higgins has long played second fiddle to Ja'Marr Chase in the otherworldly Bengals passing attack but is now on level ground with his superstar teammate. Both saw exactly 61 targets across their first seven games, and both grabbed 43 catches on those opportunities. But Higgins has been the far more efficient receiver of the two with 726 yards. That ranks second in the NFL, only to potential repeat Offensive Player of the Year winner Jaxon Smith-Njigba. This is the best version of Higgins the league has seen, and it is on pace for historic production.James Pearce Jr. to make season debut: The NFL reinstated Pearce after he served an eight-game suspension for a violation of the league's personal conduct policy, which makes him eligible to play for the first time this season in Week 9. Atlanta has been surprisingly disruptive on the defensive front without the second-year pass rusher, who faced felony charges this offseason following a domestic dispute but is on track to have those charges dropped. A unit that ranks sixth in quarterback pressure rate may climb even closer to the top of the leaderboard and perhaps improve its sack totals upon Pearce's insertion into the lineup, because he logged 10.5 sacks as a rookie despite starting only three games.Joe Burrow on MVP pace: Only two quarterbacks (Josh Allen and Brock Purdy) have shorter odds, via DraftKings Sportsbook, to win the NFL's top individual award. Burrow leads both of them in touchdowns with a league-best 20, and he is a mere 0.1 points away from the NFL lead in passer rating at 111.6. This is so far the most efficient season of Burrow's stellar career, which is a pleasant development of an offense that missed him dearly when he missed a combined 16 games over the last three seasons due to injuries. The Falcons kept Purdy in check when they upset him and the San Francisco 49ers two weeks ago, but Burrow presents an even greater challenge and has a healthier supporting cast than the one Purdy brought into the Week 7 contest.Falcons vs. Bengals predictionFans of American football in Spain are in for a treat, because this game has all the makings of a shootout. There is not an offense in the NFL that is clicking quite like the Bengals over the last three weeks, and between Burrow, Chase, Higgins, London and Robinson, five of the biggest names in football will be in action in a star-studded battle. Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. should bounce back from last week's dreadful 8-for-24 showing in the rain, so Atlanta ought to have enough juice to keep pace with a team that is averaging 36.3 points per game since Oct. 11.
In a matchup where points will be aplenty, the team with the better defense holds the edge. It is not as though Atlanta is vastly superior on that side of the ball, but it is much more reliable and is about to insert one of its projected top producers into the lineup for the first time this season. There is not a more opportune time for a disruptive pass rusher like Pearce to make his first appearance than against arguably the best quarterback in the NFL. That alone could be the difference in a high-variance matchup like this one. Pick: Falcons 34, Bengals 30

title: Amid Oregon's shortcomings in 2026, Dan Lanning is turning in his best performance yet as Ducks coach - CBS Sports
description: Oregon might fall short of a national title, but navigating a QB crisis, firing an offensive coordinator and stun
body:
Oregon might fall short of a national title, but navigating a QB crisis, firing an offensive coordinator and stunning Ohio State represents the best coaching job of Lanning's career
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:01 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        A couple of months from now, Dan Lanning might look back at an Oregon season in which the Ducks fell short of all their primary goals. There's a strong chance they won't win the Big Ten, and there's a good chance they won't even reach the College Football Playoff, let alone win a national title.And as Lanning looks back, he may realize that 2026 was his greatest season as a head coach.Lanning's criticisms as a head coach have been consistent since he first stood on the sidelines at Oregon and watched his team get decimated by Georgia 49-3 to open the 2022 season. He's a great recruiter and motivator, but he's not a game-day coach. That's why his teams come up short so often in the biggest games when they can't just "out-talent" their opposition.But if those criticisms are true, explain how Oregon is 6-3 right now after beating Ohio State 41-28 in The Horseshoe on Saturday.
Oregon's season on the brinkEverything that could go wrong for Oregon in 2026 went wrong. It started the season looking like a team that had read all the press clippings about how great it would be. The Ducks seemed to lack a sense of urgency in a close win over Boise State to open the season, and they suffered a shocking upset loss a week later against Oklahoma State.The primary concern about Oregon heading into the year had to do with having two new coordinators on both sides of the ball. They were internal promotions, not big-name hires. The concerns seemed well-founded, with both the offense and defense struggling to start.Two weeks after the Oklahoma State loss, it looked like the season would truly spiral out of control. Dante Moore took a vicious hit while sliding and was knocked out of the game against USC. The Ducks rallied and won without him, but Moore hasn't played since and is out for the year. In his first start, Dylan Raiola and the offense turned the ball over seven times in a 17-15 home loss to UCLA. That loss led to Raiola, a high-priced transfer brought in to back up Moore and await his turn to start in 2027, being benched for Brock Thomas. Thomas struggled mightily a week later against Nebraska, and then it was Raiola coming in to lead a game-winning fourth-quarter drive.
Things seemed to have settled down. The Ducks were 4-2, but still had everything to play for. Then they went on the road to face an Illinois team forced to start a true freshman at QB due to its own QB injuries. And Illinois won. The Ducks suffered their third loss of the season before the end of October. The moment Lanning changed courseIt was a perilous situation. There have been plenty of examples of teams that came into a season with high expectations and effectively quit on the season once things went south. It's become more prevalent in the transfer portal era, since not everybody in the locker room has the same connection to a program that they may have had a decade ago.
But Lanning kept his team together despite all the evidence that they were toast. He made the difficult decision to fire offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer. It was an admission of a mistake, and one plenty of coaches have refused to make because pride wouldn't let them tell the world they messed up.The following week, they found themselves down 14 points to Northwestern. Another opportunity to lay down. Instead, the Ducks fought back to beat the Wildcats 34-26. On Saturday, Ohio State came out of the gates hot and stormed out to a 14-0 lead. Another opportunity for Oregon to quit, and another offer denied. It was 38-14 by the time Ohio State scored again. Ohio Stadium had begun to empty long before. 
Now, all of a sudden, Oregon sits at 6-3 with a shot. It might not be a great one, but it's there. The Ducks are through the most difficult stretch of their schedule and will finish with home games against Michigan and Washington, with a road trip to 2-6 Michigan State in between.The offense has looked much more comfortable since the OC change. The defense has had its act together for over a month at this point. I don't know if Oregon will win out, nor do I know if it'll reach the College Football Playoff. I suspect it won't. But I've been more impressed by Dan Lanning as a head coach for how he's handled things when damn near everything that could've gone wrong did. You learn a lot more from failure than success, and Lanning has learned a whole hell of a lot in 2026.
Maybe one day the lessons of this season will help Lanning and Oregon accomplish the goals they aren't likely to accomplish this time around.

title: Lane Kiffin falls flat against Alabama as massive LSU hype crashes into reality - CBS Sports
description: A $91 million contract and the sport's priciest roster haven't translated to the big stage as the Tigers drop to
body:
A $91 million contract and the sport's priciest roster haven't translated to the big stage as the Tigers drop to 0-3 against ranked teams after another humbling against Alabama
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:00 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        When Lane Kiffin got off the bus for the Tiger Walk before the Alabama game, he was flanked by Shaquille O'Neal and Angel Reese. Kevin Costner -- Kevin freaking Costner! -- walked behind him and shook his hand. No one has brought more attention and hype to a college football program this year than Kiffin. He signed a seven-year, $91 million contract, tied with two-time national champion Kirby Smart for the second-highest in college football. According to 247Sports, his roster is the most expensive in college football, approaching $50 million. And then, Alabama walked into the building. The Field of Dreams turned into a nightmare. No. 14 LSU collapsed under the weight of expectation against No. 5 Alabama, losing 31-13 in blowout fashion. After taking a 13-10 lead in the third quarter, the Tigers allowed 21 unanswered points for Kiffin's sixth straight loss against the Crimson Tide. 
With the loss, LSU sits at 6-3 and 0-3 against teams in the CFP Rankings. Their most impressive performance is arguably a one-point loss to No. 6 Kentucky on the road. While Kiffin has raised LSU's floor, putting unranked teams into the dirt, he has no-showed against real national competition. In every high-leverage moment, Alabama smoked LSU. The Tide held LSU to a field goal after first-and-goal. They forced a missed field goal, then set up a touchdown from great field position. LSU turned it over on downs three times, including twice in the fourth quarter, and turned the ball over twice. And what makes matters worse is that Kiffin's signature offense was completely outdueled by Alabama defensive coordinator Kane Wommack. Statistically, LSU managed to put up 457 yards, but the numbers go deeper. They finished in the 19th percentile for yards per play, 20th percentile for EPA per play and 1st percentile for Explosive Play Rate, according to Game on Paper. 
Essentially, LSU didn't do anything to truly force Alabama's defense to adjust. That's a hard pill to swallow when you've built your career on being an offensive savant. Kiffin had a great run at Ole Miss, elevating the program to new heights, especially by working with the Grove Collective to improve their NIL operation. With his roster left behind, Pete Golding led Ole Miss to the national semifinals last year. Kiffin has still never actually coached a postseason game, a streak that will likely continue this year. LSU still has two more shots against No. 7 Texas and No. 13 Tennessee for ranked wins, but the Tigers team that shows up against elite teams simply isn't good enough to win both games. If they split the result, LSU would finish 8-4 with a 1-4 record against CFP Top 25 opponents. 
After the season, most of the best players on the roster will be gone to the NFL. Kiffin will have to start all over again, building through the transfer portal. For the first time since 2016, the top two recruits in Louisiana are heading out of state. Adding insult to injury, No. 3 quarterback Elijah Haven -- a Baton Rouge native -- picked Kalen DeBoer and the Tide over Kiffin. Kiffin walked into Baton Rouge with an unbelievable amount of hype, landing Vanity Fair covers and dominating the interview circuit. When he got the job, Louisiana senator John Kenny joked, all of this nonsense is worth it -- but he better win. Well, Kiffin isn't winning. And after yet another embarrassing loss to Alabama, he could be heading for a painful offseason.

title: Jeremiah Smith should skip rest of Ohio State's season, former national champion says: 'Nothing to gain' - CBS Sports
description: The Buckeyes' standout pass-catcher has more to lose than gain, according to Damien Harris
body:
The Buckeyes' standout pass-catcher has more to lose than gain, according to Damien Harris
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:23 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith needs to shut it down for the season and begin 2027 NFL Draft preparations as this cycle's top overall player, according to CBS Sports analyst and former NFL running back Damien Harris. Smith recorded seven catches for 133 yards and a touchdown in Saturday's 41-28 loss to No. 23 Oregon, one that likely detonates the 12th-ranked Buckeyes' College Football Playoff hopes as a three-loss team with three games to play. The Buckeyes have lost two straight since starting QB Julian Sayin suffered what is expected to be a season-ending injury in a win vs. Indiana. One of college football's highest-paid players (he reportedly turned down $10 million to transfer to Miami, to give you an idea), Smith holds program records for receptions, touchdowns, receiving yards and won a national championship with the Buckeyes as a freshman in 2024."We just watched Jeremiah Smith play his last snap at Ohio State," Harris said after the game."He's done. He's going to pack it up. He's not playing anymore this season. The season's gone. This isn't a CFP team, they were already on the outside looking in. He's already etched his name in history. He's got the touchdown record, he's got the reception record, he's got a national championship. He's not going to get a Heisman this year, what's there to play for?"
Harris said it's time for Smith, projected as the No. 1 overall prospect in CBS Sports' latest rankings, to look after himself and realize there's "bigger things out there" than what the rest of the season has to offer for a team that's not going to play for a Big Ten Championship and is likely outside the top 15 in Tuesday new's CFP Rankings.Cameras captured Smith noticeably frustrated in the fourth quarter of the loss to the Ducks, shouting toward his coaching staff. Freshman quarterback Luke Fahey did throw for 360 yards in the loss to Oregon, but there were times during the game where Smith's targets were inconsistent. The Buckeyes jumped out to a 14-point lead in the first half before giving up the next 31 points to Oregon.
"In my opinion, there's nothing to gain and everything to lose if you're Jeremiah Smith," Harris said. Harris played in the pre-NIL era for Nick Saban at Alabama, winning multiple national championships during his four-year career and finishing with 3,070 yards rushing and 23 touchdowns. A third-round pick in 2019, Harris rushed for 2,188 yards and 21 scores over five NFL seasons, four coming with the New England Patriots. Elite college football players have routinely skipped postseason games in recent years, but few have shut things down before the end of the regular season as a means to avoid injury. College football in some ways is more similar to the NFL now than to its pre-NIL era -- player contracts can be written to space out payments and safeguard against sit-outs, in the same way NFL players do not shut it down for self-preservation purposes when their team is eliminated from playoff contention. Ohio State has three games remaining, including the rivalry showdown against Michigan in the finale.
One of the Heisman frontrunners entering Week 10, Smith's odds considerably weakened after the Buckeyes' second straight setback. Smith entered the day second nationally in receiving yards per game, though, and has a good shot at his first Biletnikoff Award -- given annually to the nation's best receiver, a title he has unofficially held for three seasons now -- should he continue playing and should he and Fahey improve their chemistry through the end of the month.

title: NFL fines Jaquan Brisker, two others for illegal Week 8 hits that placed opponents in concussion protocol - CBS Sports
description: Each of the players on the receiving end of those collisions will miss Week 9
body:
Each of the players on the receiving end of those collisions will miss Week 9
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:01 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The NFL levied 31 fines in Week 8, which was the second most in a single week this season. Among the most notable punishments were those handed down to Pittsburgh Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker, Dallas Cowboys linebacker DeMarvion Overshown and Las Vegas Raiders safety Jeremy Chinn. Each fine was the result of a hit that led to the offensive player being placed in concussion protocol and ruled out for Week 9.Brisker owes the NFL $17,911 for a blow to the head/neck on Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson. The play occurred less than a minute and a half into the Steelers' victory and drew a roughing the passer penalty, which Brisker voiced extreme displeasure with after the game."Babying the quarterback," Brisker said. "He's laying there crying, whatever he was doing. It is what it is. I assume I'm going to get fined because if you watch it, I'm hitting him with my chest and them I'm off to the side. But he had his binky today, so they threw it out there. It is what it is."Watson briefly left the game, and Shedeur Sanders replaced him. The latter threw two passes before Watson returned to action and finished the game. Although Watson practiced in the days leading up to this Sunday's matchup against the New Orleans Saints and cleared the concussion protocol on Saturday, the Browns announced they will turn to Sanders as their Week 9 starter.
Overshown's fine is for his use of his helmet on a hit against Arizona Cardinals running back Bam Knight. He must pay $9,528. The hit jarred the ball loose from Knight's hands, and the Cowboys recovered the fumble without a penalty. The NFL reviewed the play in the wake of the game, however, and issued the fine.
Knight will not play in the Cardinals' divisional clash with the Seattle Seahawks. He did not practice this week.
Chinn sealed a Raiders win last week with an interception in the end zone, but just one play prior, he made forcible contact with New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson on a catch along the sideline, which resulted in a fine. Chinn owes $17,911 for a hit on a defenseless player. The two players' helmets collided on the play, and while Wilson stayed in the game for the Jets' final snap, he later entered concussion protocol.Wilson reported concussion symptoms the next day, and by midweek the Jets placed him in the protocol. They eventually ruled him out for this week's battle with the Kansas City Chiefs.
There have been 223 plays this season which resulted in a fine. That is 0.0113% of all plays through eight weeks. The 31 fines from Week 8 were second only to the 38 in Week 2.

An emphatic road win at Ole Miss sets up the Dawgs to reclaim the No. 1 spot, while Notre Dame's victory sends Miami sliding down the rankings
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 7, 2026

        When you have seven different games between teams that were just announced in the top 25 of the new College Football Playoff Rankings, the postseason outlook hung in the balance throughout a chaotic Week 10. The day provided some massive wins for top teams, certainly, but also yet another change at No. 1. Notre Dame's 31-24 win against Miami will open up the top spot for debate regarding the best team in college football. We will have to wait until Tuesday night to hear from the College Football Playoff Selection Committee, but fans get their first look at the new landscape with the release of an updated AP Top 25 poll on Sunday. We project that Georgia will move up into the No. 1 spot in the wake of an impressive wire-to-wire win at Ole Miss on Saturday night, edging out a Utah team that will certainly have a case with its 9-0 record and its own high-quality Week 10 win against BYU. The AP voters had a closer gap between Georgia and Miami than they did between Georgia and Utah, and those signals point to the Bulldogs keeping that margin to the tune of returning to the No. 1 spot just ahead of the Utes. As for the Fighting Irish, beating Miami provides an interesting moment in rankings analysis because of the disparity between the AP poll and the College Football Playoff Rankings. Notre Dame was slotted at No. 11 by the selection committee and in that lens, should be poised for a big move up after beating No. 1. 
The only problem? Notre Dame was already up in a top position in the eyes of the AP voters at No. 4, and that leaves much less room for a big move up in those rankings despite the impressive and much-needed win. Other winners from the ranked-on-ranked games will see some notable improvements in the AP poll, including moves up for Tennessee and Alabama after double-digit wins against other ranked SEC foes. It's going to also put a spotlight on the cut line for a top 25 ballot, as teams like Ole Miss and LSU fight for inclusion after taking their third loss of the season. Here's how we think the new AP Top 25 poll will look on Sunday after Week 10: 1. Georgia (Last week -- 2): After thrashing Ole Miss, the Bulldogs are set to return to the No. 1 spot. Georgia reached No. 1 earlier this season for a one-week residence before the upset loss to Auburn, and now that stunning, turnover-filled defeat is the lone blemish on a resume that is otherwise highlighted by wins over Alabama, Ole Miss and Florida. 
2. Utah (3): There was already one brave AP poll voter who had Utah as their No. 1 team coming into the week, and we're projecting that they'll have more company after the Utes emerged victorious in a 28-20 thriller against rival BYU. 3. Notre Dame (4): As we mentioned earlier, it's extremely difficult to know exactly how the AP voters will react to the differences in their rankings and the selection committee's decisions. In Notre Dame's case, there is an instinct to improve their position from No. 11, but voters individually don't have much room to move the Fighting Irish up on their ballots if the team was at No. 4 last week. 4. UCLA (5): The great power of the Bruins' ranking remains as Bob Chesney's crew improved to 9-0 with a win at Minnesota. The victory added to an impressive series of road performances for UCLA, and also included a wild second half showing from quarterback Ty Dieffenbach. The Bruins' starter finished with 303 passing yards and three touchdowns on just eight completions behind explosive pass plays of 75, 75, 54 and 27 yards, with three of those coming after halftime. 
5. Miami (1): A close loss on the road to another top team has its limits for rankings punishment. That is especially true when it's early November, the first loss of the season, and it also comes without your star wide receiver because of a recent injury. Miami could fall lower, but it's hard to imagine an 8-1 team with obvious quality loss dropping behind multiple two-loss teams. 6. Alabama (9): The AP voters already had Alabama as the top two-loss team in the country last week, but that status is now undeniable after the Crimson Tide pulled away from LSU for a 31-13 win in Baton Rouge. Kalen DeBoer's team got off to a strong start and stayed in control most of the afternoon, then finished on a 21-0 run the moment LSU got its first lead of the game. The win adds to victories against Kentucky and South Carolina, building a solid resume even against other teams with fewer losses.  7. Indiana (6): The Hoosiers were off in Week 10 and will be back in action next week at home against USC. 
8. Texas (10): There is not a ton of room for upward movement after a hard-fought road win at Missouri, but the Longhorns definitely strengthened their resume with the road win. Though the Tigers could fall from the top 25 after the defeat, it's still a quality win that will bolster Texas' status as a top-10 team.  9. Tennessee (16): This is admittedly a big jump up in the rankings but one that could be warranted after both a 34-6 point win against Kentucky and also the success of Alabama at LSU. The Vols could ultimately be held back from jumping ahead of Alabama because of the head-to-head loss to Texas, but anything between No. 6 and No. 10 is fair game for a Tennessee team that is 7-2 with a pair of top-end wins against teams that were ranked in the top 10 at the time. 10. Texas Tech (13): The Red Raiders needed some late-game heroics to hold on against West Virginia, but the 53-48 shootout win should keep them steady in the rankings. How Texas Tech's 8-1 resume stacks up against some of the other two-loss SEC teams in this range will vary from voter to voter, but in the consensus the team is probably set for a move up in the rankings close to the top 10.   
11. Wake Forest (14): Starting quarterback Gio Lopez was able to spend an extra week getting healthy for the final push of the season as his Demon Deacon teammates crushed FCS Merrimack 77-0. 12. BYU (7): The Cougars could end up getting credit for their competitiveness in a 28-20 loss at Utah that had more than a couple of self-inflicted wounds preventing the upset rivalry win. BYU had a 20-0 run in the middle of this game but saw its last effort end on a Bear Bachmeier interception that dropped the Cougars to 7-2 overall. The win against Notre Dame clearly serves as the strongest resume point for BYU, but the playoff conversation in general is getting late early with two conference losses and few quality win opportunities left. 13. Kentucky (8): Wins against LSU and South Carolina keep the floor pretty high for Kentucky, but it should be noted the AP voters were a bit lower on the Wildcats than the selection committee. So the drop to No. 13 is really just a five-spot drop for the AP voters, while it would be a seven-spot drop from their CFP Rankings placement of No. 6. 
14. Houston (17): The Cougars improved to 7-2 after surviving a good test from Cincinnati, holding on for a 31-24 win behind three total touchdowns from Conner Weigman. Houston is working with a bit of a quality loss resume, with unranked Oklahoma State as its best win, but their quality has held up across nine games, and the only two losses are each by one score to other ranked teams on the road (Utah, Texas Tech). 15. Oregon (NR): The Ducks were ranked in the College Football Playoff Selection Committee top 25 and will absolutely be set for a return to the AP poll after a 41-28 win in Columbus against Ohio State. It's unclear whether the reaction will be stronger for Oregon after the win or the Buckeyes after the loss, but a 6-3 record with wins over Ohio State, USC and Boise State is a solid resume for top 25 consideration. 16. USC (18): The Trojans were off in Week 10 and will be back in action next week at Indiana. 
17. Ohio State (11): The AP voters are not tasked with the same injury consideration protocols the in the same way as the College Football Playoff Selection Committee, and thus we're not projecting Saturday's loss to Oregon to be treated as anything other than a defeat to another Big Ten title contender. Wins against Indiana and Iowa serve as the best buffer to keep Ohio State from a rankings free-fall.18. Boise State (20): The Broncos did not have starting quarterback Maddux Madsen due to injury, but that did not stop the team from putting 64 points on the board against a Colorado State team that has gotten picked apart in Pac-12 play. Now 8-1 overall, Boise State's attention turns to its home stretch of the season, which includes the first-ever Pac-12 flex week at the end of November with a matchup yet to be determined for Week 13. 19. Iowa (21): A road test at Northwestern proved to be yet another resume point for an Iowa team that continues to handle its business. The Hawkeyes have wins over Northwestern, Wisconsin and Michigan, and just two losses on the season to Ohio State and Minnesota. It's not a resume that overwhelms voters, but in a season that lacks consistency there is something comforting about Iowa's 7-2 profile. 
20. New Mexico (22): The Lobos are going to keep the historic AP ranking the program achieved last week, but the margins around the cut line are slim enough to be concerned about giving up a spot in the consensus rankings. Teams like Oregon and Ohio State occupying spaces in the 20s make it tough for New Mexico to win some of those tiebreaker resume debates, even if their 8-1 record is two games better than those preseason title picks.  21. South Carolina (23): The winning streak continues with South Carolina now up to four wins in a row since starting 0-3 in SEC play. The Gamecocks' victory against Texas A&M in Columbia isn't going to move the voters individually, but the collective appreciation of South Carolina's late-season form will continue to get respect, and the win against Tennessee certainly holds more weight now for the argument that this should be among the highest-ranked three-loss teams in the country. 22. Ole Miss (12): Not only did the Rebels lose in a great opportunity with Georgia in town, but Ole Miss' resume took a hit with the results from SEC play in Week 10. Wins against both LSU and Missouri take on less weight after both of those teams are headed down, if not out, in the rankings, as Ole Miss seems destined to get pinned with similar three-loss teams near the edge of the top 25. 
23. Arizona (24): Unranked by the College Football Playoff Selection Committee but ranked by the AP voters last week, the Wildcats are going to be right on the cut line after needing a late onside kick and field goal to avoid an upset against TCU. Arizona does stand out with its 7-2 record, but its best win came against Cincinnati, and it's 0-2 against other ranked teams this season. 24. LSU (15): There is an argument to drop LSU from the top 25 based on an absence of high-quality wins, but we aren't projecting that reaction from the AP voters. Lane Kiffin's Tigers will have an opportunity to win their way back up the rankings with matchups against Texas and Tennessee in the coming weeks, but for now, LSU has just three SEC wins against opponents who have a combined 6-14 record in conference play. Voters might not drop LSU from No. 15 all the way out for losing a national title contender, but the Tigers are absolutely on notice if they can't win out. 25. SMU (NR): The Mustangs improved to 7-2 with an eye-popping 51-28 win against Virginia Tech on Friday night in Dallas. The victory sets up the potential for an appearance in the top 25 ahead of a massive showdown with Wake Forest in Week 11. Projected to drop out: No. 19 Missouri, No. 25 Florida
